text: `click.prompt` (and `confirm`) catches `KeyboardInterrupt` and `EOFError` and raises `click.exceptions.Abort` (i.e. `click.Abort`). See src/click/termui.py lines 144-150 (prompt) and 236-237 (confirm); the docstring says "the function will catch it and raise a :exc:`Abort` exception."
It is set to the string `"ascii"` (`fs_enc = "ascii"` in the `except Exception:` block of `_verify_python_env` in src/click/_unicodefun.py).

Fixed. In `Option.__init__` (src/click/core.py), the auto-default `False` for flags was applied even when the option was declared `required=True`, so a required flag was never considered missing. Changed:

    if is_flag and default_is_missing and not self.required:
        self.default = False

Now `--flag` with `is_flag=True, required=True` and no default raises `Missing option '--flag'.` (exit code 2) when omitted, and works normally when given. Full test suite still passes: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.
#1 is fixed and verified (required flags now report "Missing option '--flag'."; full suite green).

#4 still in progress — I've located it (echo/ProgressBar/pager failing when sys.stdout/stderr is None, e.g. pythonw); implementing the None-safe stream handling in _compat.py, utils.py and _termui_impl.py now. ETA ~8 min.
`_verify_python_env` raises a `RuntimeError` (built with "\n\n".join(extra) as the message) when `fs_enc == "ascii"`.
`style` raises a `TypeError` — e.g. `TypeError(f"Unknown color {fg!r}")` when `_interpret_color(fg)` raises `KeyError` (same for `bg`).
`echo` is imported in src/click/__init__.py from the `.utils` module (`from .utils import echo`).
It returns `"Invalid value: {message}"` formatted with the exception's message, i.e. `_("Invalid value: {message}").format(message=self.message)`.

#4 done. echo/progressbar/pager no longer crash when sys.stdout/sys.stderr are None: _make_cached_stream_func returns None for a None stream, echo returns early, and ProgressBar/pager fall back to a dummy StringIO. Verified with sys.stdout=sys.stderr=None; full suite green.

#8 still in progress: the bug is that an option with `flag_value` ignores its envvar (the env value is never converted to the flag value). Implementing the fix in Option.consume_value now. ETA ~6 min.

#11 done. `click.argument`'s decorator popped `cls` from the shared `attrs` dict, so a second use of the same decorator fell back to the base `Argument` class. It now copies attrs (like `option` does), so the custom class is preserved on every use. Full suite green.
It returns the hints joined with `" / "`, each wrapped in `repr()`: `" / ".join(repr(x) for x in param_hint)`. (For a plain string it returns the string unchanged.)
It returns the `color` argument unchanged (`if color is not None: return color`); only when it is `None` does it fall back to the current context's `color` (or `None` if there is no context).

#15 done. `Path(resolve_path=True)` did `os.readlink(rv)` when the path was a symlink, which returned the raw (possibly relative) link target instead of the resolved path. It now uses `pathlib.Path(rv).resolve()` (via os.fsdecode), so symlinks resolve correctly on all platforms while path_type=bytes/Path still work. Full suite green.
It returns `None` (the `except (AttributeError, IndexError)` branch only raises `RuntimeError` when `silent` is false).
It raises a `TypeError` — `_unpack_args` raises `TypeError("Cannot have two nargs < 0")` when more than one entry in the nargs spec is negative.
